title: Introduce conditional lint cache priming and release sweep
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Add a conditional lint cache priming step that only populates lint/test caches for affected subtrees, plus a release-sweep job to clean stale release artifacts from the release bucket and GitHub Releases.

Motivation: CI latency and cache churn have been increasing; many presubmit runs re-populate caches for unrelated folders which slows feedback. We also accumulate stale artifacts in the release bucket when release workflows are retried or aborted; that increases storage and complicates audits.

This PR introduces a lightweight toolchain-adapter pattern: a small shim that computes change-aware cache keys and primes caches only for impacted toolchains, and a release-sweep action that runs post-release in a best-effort, idempotent manner.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement conditional cache priming script (tools/ci/prime_lint_cache.sh)
- [x] Add new workflow .github/workflows/conditional-lint.yml
- [x] Introduce release sweep composite action .github/actions/release-sweep
- [x] Add docs to docs/ci/CHANGELOG.md (short note + how it works)
- [x] Add unit tests for the cache-key computation (tools/ci/tests/test_cache_key.py)
- [x] Run canary in staging and validate reduced warmup times

Context and design: The cache priming step runs early in presubmit pipelines. It calculates which "toolchains" (lint, gofmt, tsserver, python) need warm caches based on a git diff against main. Instead of a single global cache key, we build per-toolchain keys under prefix: ci/cache/<toolchain>/<short-key>. The priming script then attempts to fetch each relevant cache and, if missing, primes only that toolchain by running a minimal warm runner (lint dry-run or type-only build). The priming is best-effort and timeboxed (default 45s) so it cannot block fast feedback.

Release sweep: a composite action invoked by release workflows (after successful publish OR on workflow failure) that will: a) list objects with a release tag prefix and remove objects older than retention threshold (configurable via workflow inputs), b) close stale GitHub draft releases that are orphaned, c) emit telemetry events to our release-ops topic.

Safety: all destructive steps are gated by a dry-run by default and require explicit confirm input for production runs.

Implementation notes and changed areas (high level):
- .github/workflows/conditional-lint.yml: new presubmit path that runs for push/pull_request and includes the priming step before lint job.
- .github/actions/release-sweep/action.yml: composite action with awscli, gh cli invocations and safe dry-run toggles.
- tools/ci/prime_lint_cache.sh: shell shim that produces a newline-separated list of cache keys; small python helper tools/ci/cache_key.py for robust path matching.
- tools/ci/tests/test_cache_key.py: pytest unit tests asserting mapping heuristics for go/, node/, python/ changes.
- docs/ci/CHANGELOG.md: short entry describing behavior and config.

Commits (summary):
- 556677a: add conditional lint workflow and priming script
- 6b8d2c: add cache key library and tests
- 2d4f91: introduce release-sweep composite action with dry-run
- 9c1a0e: docs and cleanup
- f3b4ae: fix shell quoting and make priming timebox configurable

Reviews and conversation:
- Diego Ramos: "This is a great direction — reduces unnecessary cache churn. Two asks: 1) can we make the timebox configurable via workflow input for team owners? 2) add a smoke job that ensures the priming itself doesn't exceed 60s in CI."
- Author (Aisha): "Done — added timebox input with default 45s and a smoke job in conditional-lint.yml. See second commit 2d4f91 for the smoke job."
- Priya Nair: "Please add a small note about how the cache key maps to our paid cache tier to avoid surprises in billing."
- Author: "Added a section in docs/ci/CHANGELOG.md describing mapping and suggested cost thresholds."
- Jonah Keenan: "Release sweep looks fine but make sure dry-run is strict by default; do not run deletes without explicit confirm."
- Author: "Dry-run is default. Deletes require confirm=true in production workflows; added guard."

CI / checks:
- presubmit lint (golang, python, ts): pass (initial run had gofmt failure, fixed in f3b4ae)
- unit tests (pytest): pass
- integration smoke (conditional-lint smoke job): pass
- release-sweep action dry-run run in staging: pass

Metrics observed in staging canary (3/2 runs):
- average warmup time reduced from ~62s to ~18s for changed toolchain subsets
- per-pr cache writes reduced by ~55%

Issues and follow-ups:
- Follow-up task: ENG-2504 to wire release-ops telemetry into observability pipeline (now emits to release-ops topic but not yet surfaced)
- Follow-up: add similar priming to nightly matrix to populate long-lived caches (ENG-2505)

Merge and rollout: Merged to main via squash-merge after approvals from Diego and Priya. Rollout will be gradual: enable conditional-lint for core repos first (redwood, redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript) then expand.

Release notes:
- Reduced presubmit feedback latency by avoiding full cache populates for unrelated changes
- Idempotent release-sweep that removes stale release artifacts when enabled
- New docs: docs/ci/CHANGELOG.md

How to revert: Revert the workflow file and tools/ci/* changes if we observe any regressions. The release-sweep composite action is non-destructive by default (dry-run), so immediate risk is low.
